newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Lufthansa H1 passenger numbers grow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Lufthansa H1 passenger numbers grow.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG on Wednesday said its passenger numbers rose 5.7 percent to 20.8 million in the first half of 1997 from 19.682 million a year earlier.
Its passenger load factor in the first half was 71.7 percent, up from 67.6 percent a year ago, in line with its forecasts.
Lufthansa added that yields in its cargo business were much improved on the previous year.

"The passenger load factor was fully in line with our plans. Yields in the cargo business were much better than last year," Rolf-Dieter Grass, head of Lufthansa's investor relations department, told Reuters.
"These figures are not so surprising -- the first half was strongly influenced by CityLine and Condor -- and I would say they are in line," Andreas Schmidt, analyst at BZW in Frankfurt, said.
Cargo and post tonnage fell slightly in the first half to 812,400 tonnes, compared with 815,700, but yield per kilometre was clearly higher, Grass said.
The main rise in passenger numbers came from Lufthansa's CityLine service, where passenger numbers grew 24.2 percent to 1.8 million.
Around 3.2 million passengers flew on Lufthansa's holiday airline subsidiary, Condor, an increase of 10.7 percent.
Lufthansa said the number of flights grew 6.5 percent in the six months to around 309,000. This related chiefly to more flights at Lufthansa Cargo and Lufthansa CityLine.
Capacity increased by around two percentage points to 70.3 percent.
